findings.summary: A file outside the expected deliverables list changed: crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs.
findings.evidence: The LIMIT constant changed from 'No file outside README.md changed' to 'No file outside README.md and CHANGELOG.md changed'. The edit is needed because those scope tests pass the limit through the real gate, which now refuses it. It was in the planned files and D166 and the CHANGELOG mention it, but it is not in the deliverables list.

findings.summary: The check departs from the accepted reading's design in three places, all documented: a CHANGELOG.md deliverable alone does not satisfy the check, a crates/ test deliverable alone does not satisfy the config half, and out_of_scope items are not read as limits.
findings.evidence: The reading said a limit passes if it 'list[s] CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable ... or name[s] it in the limit', and that a config change passes with 'a crates/ test deliverable or ... `Consumers:`'. The code requires CHANGELOG.md in the limit's words and a Consumers line. D166 explains each change: `ensure_changelog` makes the deliverable test inert, an unrelated test deliverable is no answer, and verification reads criteria only. All three make the rule stricter or match verification, so none weakens it.

findings.summary: The config half forces the reader to answer who loads the config but cannot verify the answer: `Consumers: none found` passes without any search.
findings.evidence: D166 lists this as a known miss. Scanning repo contents was out_of_scope in the reading. The check does verify that every consumer path the reader names is a deliverable.

findings.summary: The producer raised the byte limit on the reading-rules section from 2900 to 3150 to fit the new rule line.
findings.evidence: `assert!(section.len() < 3150, ...)`; the comment says the measured size is 3045. The reading allowed one short line in briefs.rs, and the reader prompt text is unchanged.

summary: The change fixes the problem where the reading is accepted. It adds a new check, `check_scope_limit`, called from one `step!` line in `refusing_check`. A change reading is refused when one of its criteria limits which files may change and that limit (1) names its allowed files but leaves out CHANGELOG.md and does not say "the deliverables", or (2) the reading changes athena.toml or defaults.toml without a `Consumers:` assumption. That line must name only paths that are deliverables, or say "none found" or "unchanged". Both the gate and verification now read a limit through the same matcher (`change_limit`), so they cannot read one sentence two ways. The doc comment, the CHANGELOG entry and the new decision record D166 name the root cause, the failure class and both jobs. I ran the targeted tests and all pass: 8 `scope_limit_*` unit tests, the 23 refusal-corpus tests and the matcher test. Athena's fails-without runs show the unit tests do not compile and the corpus fails when the fix is reverted. The recorded CI results show fmt, clippy and `cargo test --locked` pass. The replay of past readings newly refused 1 of 50, a defaults.toml reading, which is the intended effect. The change departs from the accepted reading in three places, and D166 records each one with its reason. A CHANGELOG.md deliverable alone does not satisfy the check, because `ensure_changelog` always adds that deliverable before the gate. An unrelated crates/ test deliverable alone does not satisfy the config half. Out-of-scope items are not read as limits. All three make the rule stricter or match how verification reads limits, so none is harmful. One file outside the deliverables list changed: run/tests.rs, a single test constant that the new check requires. That is a minor scope finding.
